public_rationale: Research documents continuing spatial errors, and intervention research shows that some improvements transfer beyond trained tasks. Neither establishes the claimed sequence of isolated fixes followed by new failures caused by inadequate generalization. The evidence does not justify calling the complete causal claim supported or contradicted.
limitations: Spatial reasoning studies cover only part of commonsense reasoning.
Partial generalization is compatible with continued lack of broad reliability.
No numerical definition of robust is supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM commonsense failure examples keep appearing because no robust solution has been found, even though individual examples can be fixed.

statement.excerpt: Any one example can be fixed, but examples keep rolling in because no robust solution has been found.
statement.document_title: AI still lacks “common” sense, 70 years later

from_speaker: Any one example can be fixed
because no robust solution has been found
our_interpretation: In context, examples refers to LLM commonsense failures, especially physical and spatial failures.
A robust solution means dependable generalization to new problems rather than success only on previously identified examples.
Any one example can be fixed is read as the practical possibility of correcting individual cases, not a formal theorem about every conceivable input.
The causal proposition is that fixes fail to generalize adequately, explaining continued failures.
The ongoing state is assigned to late 2024 through the publication date, 2025-01-05.
criteria.support_condition: Before-and-after evaluations show correction of individual commonsense failures but recurring failures on new variants, with controls connecting that persistence to inadequate generalization.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A validated method corrects individual cases and reliably generalizes across diverse held-out commonsense tasks, or controlled evidence establishes another explanation for the continuing failures.

evidence.explanation: PolyMATH documents spatial and reasoning errors in contemporary multimodal models. It does not follow individual fixes over time or establish why new failures appear; precise experimental dates are also unspecified.

Sparkle reports transfer from training basic spatial capabilities to more complex and different visual tasks. This cautions against assuming improvements merely patch isolated cases, but it does not demonstrate a comprehensive commonsense solution.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled studies tracking specific commonsense corrections and performance on fresh variants in the same contemporary models, with evidence separating inadequate generalization from other causes of failure.
